title: Beyond Clumsy Agentic Tool Calling: How Cueing and Spotting Make the Difference
abstract: arXiv:2611.19275v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: LLM-based task-oriented agents depend on tools to interact with their environments, but may overlook execution feedback, repeat ineffective calls, or persist with unproductive strategies. These behaviors can hinder agents' ability to use tools autonomously and sustain task progress. We characterize tool-use symptoms at two temporal granularities: local clumsy tool-use behaviors and tool-use detours spanning multiple interactions. Towards greater autonomy in tool use, we present ToolPulse, an online middleware supporting autonomous tool use through cueing and spotting. ToolPulse tracks execution state and temporal interaction patterns, monitoring proposed calls before dispatch and inspecting execution feedback prior to the agent resumes reasoning. It combines state-based rules, semantic sequence analysis, and interaction-feature similarity to identify intervention opportunities and provide verbal reminders, structured feedback, or context

translated_title: 超越笨拙的智能体工具调用：提示与识别如何带来改变
translated_abstract: 基于大语言模型（LLM）的任务型智能体依赖工具与环境进行交互，但可能忽视执行反馈、重复无效调用，或固执地坚持低效策略。这些行为会削弱智能体自主使用工具并持续推动任务进展的能力。我们从两个时间粒度刻画了工具使用症状：局部的笨拙工具使用行为，以及跨越多次交互的工具使用弯路。为了实现更自主的工具使用，我们提出了ToolPulse——一个支持自主工具使用的在线中间件，其核心是提示与识别机制。ToolPulse跟踪执行状态与时间交互模式，在调用分发之前监控拟议的调用，并在智能体恢复推理之前检查执行反馈。它将基于状态的规则、语义序列分析和交互特征相似性相结合，以识别干预时机，并提供言语提醒、结构化反馈或上下文……
tldr: 本文提出在线中间件ToolPulse，通过提示与识别机制监测智能体的笨拙工具调用与跨交互的工具使用弯路，并在调用前后及时注入提醒、结构化反馈或上下文，从而显著提升LLM智能体自主使用工具的能力。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces ToolPulse, an online middleware that enables more autonomous tool use in LLM-based agents by cueing and spotting—monitoring proposed calls and execution feedback to detect clumsy tool-use behaviors and tool-use detours, and delivering timely verbal reminders, structured feedback, or context.
